sections.text: Jean Baudrillard (1929-2007) argued that contemporary culture has lost its relationship to any underlying reality. We no longer represent reality -- we produce simulations that replace it. The map precedes the territory. The image no longer refers to anything real; it is "its own pure simulacrum." This is not relativism or skepticism -- it is a specific diagnosis of a historical condition produced by media saturation and consumer capitalism.

```
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                  BAUDRILLARD'S FRAMEWORK                         |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                                  |
|  CENTRAL CLAIM:                                                  |
|  Postmodern society has entered a condition of "hyperreality"    |
|  where simulations precede and replace reality.                  |
|                                                                  |
|  PROGRESSION:                                                    |
|  Representation --> Simulation --> Hyperreality                  |
|                                                                  |
|  KEY CONCEPTS:                                                   |
|  Simulacrum: A copy without an original                          |
|  Hyperreality: More real than real                               |
|  Sign value: Value of images/signs in a sign system             |
|  Implosion: Collapse of distinctions                             |
|                                                                  |
|  KEY WORKS:                                                      |
|  The System of Objects (1968)                                    |
|  Simulacra and Simulation (1981)                                 |
|  The Gulf War Did Not Take Place (1991)                          |
|  America (1986)                                                  |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
